name: QMP6988 barometric pressure sensor
description: QST QMP6988 digital barometric pressure (30–110 kPa, ±3.9 Pa relative, ±100 Pa absolute) and temperature (-40 to 85 °C, ±2 °C) sensor with a 24-bit ADC and per-chip OTP calibration, read over I2C. The unit has an HT7533 3.3 V regulator and BSS138 level shifters, with 4.7 kΩ pull-ups on its SDA/SCL connector side to the unit's supply pin. Sold as: M5Stack Unit Mini BPS v1.1 (SKU U090-B, QMP6988), 4-pin HY2.0-4P Grove connector GND, 5V, SDA, SCL, I2C address 0x70 (SDO tied to GND in M5Stack's schematic; the product page says 0x56), supplied with a 5 cm Grove cable.
eli5: Feels how hard the air is pressing down, so your board can tell the weather is changing or how high up it is, and it also reports the temperature.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (black wire of the Grove cable)

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply, 5 V nominal (red wire). An HT7533 regulator makes 3.3 V for the QMP6988. The SDA/SCL pull-ups go to this pin, so on an ESP32 or Pico feed it 3.3 V (the regulator then passes about 3.2 V) to keep the I2C lines at 3.3 V.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (yellow wire), 4.7 kΩ pull-up to the 5V pin, level-shifted to the chip

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (white wire), 4.7 kΩ pull-up to the 5V pin, level-shifted to the chip

supplierQuery: M5Stack Unit Mini BPS v1.1 QMP6988 U090-B
buildNotes: Grove wire colours on M5Stack cables: black GND, red 5V, yellow SDA, white SCL. Use a Grove-to-jumper lead for a breadboard.

The unit's SDA/SCL pull-ups (4.7 kΩ) go to its 5V pin. On a 3.3 V board (ESP32, Pico) feed the 5V pin from 3V3 so the bus never sees 5 V; the HT7533 still gives the QMP6988 about 3.2 V (it needs 1.71–3.6 V).
Address: 0x70 (SDO to GND per M5Stack's schematic and Arduino example); the product page lists 0x56 (SDO high). Run i2c.scan() and use whichever answers. Chip id 0x5C at register 0xD1.

Read the 25 calibration bytes at 0xA0–0xB8 once, then for each reading write CTRL_MEAS (0xF4), wait for the conversion (33.7 ms typical at ultra-high accuracy) and read 6 bytes from 0xF7: pressure then temperature, 24 bits each, MSB first, minus 2^23.
Compute temperature first (Tr in 1/256 °C), then pressure in Pa with the datasheet's polynomial. Do not linearise it.
Keep the sensor out of direct airflow and away from the regulator; draughts make the pressure reading jump.

solve.formula: Dt = RT - 8388608; Tr = a0 + a1*Dt + a2*Dt^2; Dp = RP - 8388608; b00 + bt1*Tr + bp1*Dp + b11*Tr*Dp + bt2*Tr^2 + bp2*Dp^2 + b12*Dp*Tr^2 + b21*Dp^2*Tr + bp3*Dp^3

driver.code:
# QMP6988 barometric pressure & temperature sensor (QST), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the QST QMP6988 datasheet rev C: chip id 0x5C at 0xD1, soft reset 0xE6 -> 0xE0,
# 25 OTP compensation bytes at 0xA0-0xB8, forced-mode measurement via CTRL_MEAS (0xF4),
# 24-bit raw pressure at 0xF7-0xF9 and temperature at 0xFA-0xFC (MSB first), and the
# datasheet's compensation formulas (section 4.3).
import time

_CHIP_ID = 0xD1
_RESET = 0xE0
_DEVICE_STAT = 0xF3
_CTRL_MEAS = 0xF4
_IIR = 0xF1
_PRESS_TXD2 = 0xF7
_COE = 0xA0

# Conversion factors K = A + S * OTP / 32767 (datasheet table, section 4.3): name -> (offset in OTP block, A, S)
_K = (
    ('bt1', 2, 1.00e-1, 9.10e-2),
    ('bt2', 4, 1.20e-8, 1.20e-6),
    ('bp1', 6, 3.30e-2, 1.90e-2),
    ('b11', 8, 2.10e-7, 1.40e-7),
    ('bp2', 10, -6.30e-10, 3.50e-10),
    ('b12', 12, 2.90e-13, 7.60e-13),
    ('b21', 14, 2.10e-15, 1.20e-14),
    ('bp3', 16, 1.30e-16, 7.90e-17),
    ('a1', 20, -6.30e-3, 4.30e-4),
    ('a2', 22, -1.90e-11, 1.20e-10),
)


def _s16(b, i):
    v = (b[i] << 8) | b[i + 1]
    return v - 65536 if v & 0x8000 else v


def _s20(v):
    return v - 0x100000 if v & 0x80000 else v


class QMP6988:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x70):
        """addr: 0x70 with SDO tied to GND, 0x56 with SDO tied to VDDIO."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        cid = self._r(_CHIP_ID, 1)[0]
        if cid != 0x5C:
            raise OSError('QMP6988 not found (chip id 0x%02x)' % cid)
        self._w(_RESET, 0xE6)       # soft reset, then the chip reloads its OTP
        time.sleep_ms(10)           # power-on/reset start-up time is at most 10 ms
        c = self._r(_COE, 25)       # 0xA0 ... 0xB8
        k = {}
        for name, i, a, s in _K:
            k[name] = a + s * _s16(c, i) / 32767
        # a0 and b00 are 20-bit two's complement offsets in 20Q16 format (value / 16)
        k['b00'] = _s20((c[0] << 12) | (c[1] << 4) | (c[24] >> 4)) / 16
        k['a0'] = _s20((c[18] << 12) | (c[19] << 4) | (c[24] & 0x0F)) / 16
        self.k = k
        self._w(_IIR, 0x00)         # IIR filter off

    def _r(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def read(self):
        """One forced-mode measurement. Returns (pressure in Pa, temperature in degC)."""
        # Ultra high accuracy preset: temperature average x4 (011), pressure average x32 (110), forced mode (01)
        self._w(_CTRL_MEAS, (0b011 << 5) | (0b110 << 2) | 0b01)
        time.sleep_ms(34)           # 33.7 ms typical
        for _ in range(20):
            if not self._r(_DEVICE_STAT, 1)[0] & 0x08:   # bit 3 'measure' clears when data is stored
                break
            time.sleep_ms(5)
        d = self._r(_PRESS_TXD2, 6)
        dp = ((d[0] << 16) | (d[1] << 8) | d[2]) - 8388608
        dt = ((d[3] << 16) | (d[4] << 8) | d[5]) - 8388608
        k = self.k
        tr = k['a0'] + k['a1'] * dt + k['a2'] * dt * dt          # temperature in 1/256 degC
        pr = (k['b00'] + k['bt1'] * tr + k['bp1'] * dp + k['b11'] * tr * dp
              + k['bt2'] * tr * tr + k['bp2'] * dp * dp + k['b12'] * dp * tr * tr
              + k['b21'] * dp * dp * tr + k['bp3'] * dp * dp * dp)  # pressure in Pa
        return pr, tr / 256

    def pressure(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[1]

    def altitude(self, sea_level_pa=101325.0):
        """Approximate altitude in metres from the barometric formula."""
        return 44330.0 * (1.0 - (self.read()[0] / sea_level_pa) ** 0.1903)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qmp6988 import QMP6988

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
addr = 0x70 if 0x70 in i2c.scan() else 0x56
sensor = QMP6988(i2c, addr)
while True:
    p, t = sensor.read()
    print('P=%.2f hPa T=%.1f C' % (p / 100, t))
    time.sleep_ms(500)
